title: Pot, Thelonious Monk and the preaching impulse
summary: Johnston describes being told she must be high to appreciate Monk. Gil calls this preaching by people who need reinforcement.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I was wondering though if you are aware of distortions which that have occurred in your writing when you view it later if you have worked or maybe while you were smoking. you don't smoke that much.
I don't remember really. (What do you mean, with it or without)?
Oh, without. Some people took me to hear Thelonious Monk? not so long ago at the Village, at Vanguard. And that's where you're going by the way, isn't it?
I'm going to the Village Gate.
Oh you're going to the Village Gate, alright. But in any case, they tried to insisted that I smoked some pot before I......
Oh I remember you telling me that, right. You went up to his through the apartment or something?

Yes. And I didn't finish it what I started to tell you down there. The thing that disturbed me was that I was told that if I didn't, I would not be able to appreciate his music fully. Well it seems to me that this is some kind of .....
A bit presumptuous wasn't it?
Yes. Yes, indeed it is. That's one thing. The other thing I think it's quite a disservice to a composer, or a performer to say that you have to be stoned in order to appreciate what he's doing.
Well when people talk like that they're only talking about themselves really. You know what I mean. That's a form of preaching really to tell
you a thing like that. That's like preaching isn't it?
Of course, of course.

Well one thing I've discovered about preaching most of the time, is that when you get there you stop preaching. If something exists that you need, or need to believe in, something like that, enough, and it takes care of you and you aren't afraid of it. You have no doubt or you don't need to gather to do it with the gang on the corner or you don't need to do it so you consistently think about it. You don't preach any more. That goes for religion. People who preach need to because they need to be reinforced themselves.
Yes, yes. I guess this sense of this proselyting, seems to me that they need to be enforced there.
That's what I mean. They are really not there themselves.

And even after that evening at the club listening to Thelonious Monk I was thoroughly convinced that I enjoyed him far more than they did because by the time they had their vodkas and whatever else they were drinking and they smoked pot without taking a break all night long, so finally
they were out of it, I'm still very much with it. (LAUGHTER). And listening to what he was doing.
People are smoking in public now.
Well this is what was going on there.
Oh it was?
Oh yes, oh yes.
